summary: A better-than-expected April jobs report and a tenuous U.S.-Iran ceasefire drove equities higher Friday, with the S&P 500 closing at a record 7,399. Surging gas prices tied to the Iran conflict sent consumer sentiment to a new low in early May, keeping energy costs elevated and suppressing gold's safe-haven bid even as stocks grind to new highs.
tweet: A strong April jobs report and an Iran ceasefire holding at the margins pushed the S&P 500 to records — but surging gas prices have cratered consumer sentiment, splitting risk appetite across assets.
